prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architecture and active sites

statement.case_for: I keep B003 after hearing the full first round, because none of the arguments against it was about the science and the arguments against the alternatives were about unsettled points. Organic structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and engineered acid and Lewis-acid sites let chemists choose a pore and place an active site, and that principle is now confirmed by decades of independent diffraction and microscopy, not by a single group's claim. Corma (design and industrial transfer), Zones (structure-directing agents and the SSZ family) and Davis (new frameworks, Lewis-acid and hierarchical zeolites) have distinct, documented contributions. It is the only candidate in the first round where maturity, mechanism and attribution are all reasonably settled and where there is no overlap with a prize from the last six years. I accept that a prize on a mature industrial field would need a citation that stresses the design concept, not the industrial scale.
statement.case_against: Credit is diffuse. Jihong Yu, Tsapatsis and the structure-solution community are excluded by a three-name cut, and the novelty story for a general audience is weaker than for degraders or editors. Support is thin: one member prefers B003 and the chair summary shows it with a single explicit supporter, so I cannot claim it is close to five votes. I am also in the same research community as the candidates through electron diffraction of zeolites, which may bias me toward the field. If the committee wants a prize in chemical biology or medicinal chemistry, B042 is my honest second choice, and I would vote for it over B050 or B052.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps targeted protein degradation (B042) first as a simple chemical idea with a coherent PROTAC to cereblon story, Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and says the clinical consequences are already visible in many programmes.
responses.response: Of the three leading nucleic-acid or modality topics, B042 is the one I find most chemically convincing, and I agree the ternary-complex equilibrium is a real chemical problem. My structural bias is that the claim holds because ternary-complex and cereblon-ligand structures were actually determined (the VHL and cereblon crystal structures and Ciulli's ternary-complex work), and that is precisely why Ciulli's exclusion worries me more than it worries you. A three-name cut of Crews, Deshaies and Handa honours the concept and the cereblon discovery but leaves out the person who made the rational design of degraders possible. I have not moved B042 to first place because no PROTAC is approved, but if the committee turns to B042, I would accept your trio provided the citation is written around E3 ligase recruitment and not around a drug class.

responses.point: Brzezinski has moved to B042 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, wants the expert reports to say what is unsettled before the citation spans both PROTACs and glues, and notes that the first PROTACs were peptidic and cell-impermeable.
responses.response: I agree with the request for a statement of what is unsettled, and I would add that the first-generation PROTACs being cell-impermeable peptides is the best argument that B042 is two stages of work, not a single discovery. The conceptual step (2001) and the drug-like step (small-molecule VHL and cereblon ligands, 2010s) have different authors. That is a stronger objection than the absence of an approved drug. Until the committee settles whether the prize rewards the concept or the chemistry that made it work, I cannot put B042 ahead of a design principle whose credit is already clear.

responses.point: Linke proposes a two-part prize, base editing to Liu alone and ionizable lipid nanoparticles to Cullis and Hope, as the best answer to the three-name cap, and concedes the overlap with the 2020 and 2023 prizes and that B042 could be the cleaner second part.
responses.response: I take the point that two parts avoid five or six names for one topic, but I do not think the two-part structure repairs the attribution problems. It removes Komor and Gaudelli, who carried out the experiments that made the adenine editor, and Anderson, Madden and MacLachlan, and it makes a prize made wholly of nucleic-acid medicine, which you accept might look like Chemistry following Medicine. You are right that the 2020 and 2023 overlaps are the issue. If the committee goes with two parts, I would rather see B042 paired with B052 than B050 with B052, since that spreads the prize across two kinds of molecular design. I also note the pairing does not need B003, and I am not proposing one.

responses.point: Chabes prefers base editing (B050) with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, argues that the adenine editor shows real chemical originality because TadA had to be evolved to act on DNA, but says his preference would yield to B042 if base editing is judged medicine or biotechnology.
responses.response: The adenine-editor point is the strongest chemical argument for B050, and I accept that evolving a deaminase to act on DNA is real enzyme engineering, not a repurposing. It still sits on a scaffold the committee honoured in 2020, and the evidence of success is editing outcomes, which are measured by sequencing, not by a new structural or mechanistic insight. Your own conditional statement suggests that the committee's choice between B050 and B042 is about framing, not about merit. I do not hold B003 against B050 on novelty, because both are novel, but on maturity and absence of overlap I rank B003 higher. I value your willingness to say what would change your mind.

responses.point: Somfai prefers palladium C-N coupling (B029) as a settled, two-person, molecule-making achievement, and argues that my 2010-overlap objection overstates redundancy because the amine-binding and beta-hydride elimination problems needed different ligand design.
responses.response: That correction is fair, and I am revising how I weigh B029: the ligand problem is not an obvious corollary of the C-C coupling prize. I still keep B003 above it, mainly because the shortlist has few settled molecule-making or materials candidates and B003 is the one with a broader structural-evidence base. Your point about the underrepresentation of core synthesis is also valid and is another reason I have not moved to a nucleic-acid or medicine configuration. I would put B029 ahead of B050 and B052 on maturity.

uncertainties: Whether three names for B003 will be accepted as fair given Yu, Tsapatsis and the structure-solution community, and whether a citation can express the design concept rather than industrial scale.
Whether B003 can attract any vote beyond mine, since no other member lists it as preferred or alternative.
Whether B042 is one coherent chemical idea or two (PROTAC concept and drug-like degraders, plus molecular glues), and whether Ciulli should replace Handa as the third name.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug is still a reason to hold B042 back at the time of the vote.
statement.conflict_note: My electron-diffraction work on zeolites places me in the same community as the B003 candidates, and I have probably cited or interacted with them, but I have no documented collaboration with Corma, Davis or Zones. Yu and Tsapatsis, who are outside my three-name cut, are also in this community. I have no tie to B042, B050, B052, B024, B029 or B015 beyond scientific awareness. My Stockholm University colleagueship with Secretary Brzezinski is not relevant to any shortlisted ballot.
